page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition

lines.text: Vivipary: seeds germinate on the mother plant

lines: The seed germinates while it is still
attached to the mother plant, before it
steps.why: The defining point is WHERE germination happens: on the mother plant itself, before the seed is shed.
common_mistakes: Writing 'seeds germinate early' without saying they are still on the mother plant.
Confusing vivipary with parthenocarpy (fruit formation without fertilization).
steps.memory_tip: Vivi = alive (as in viviparous animals): the seed leaves the plant already germinated and growing.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line + one supporting line is enough.

steps.label: The example
lines: The seedling grows out of the fruit on
the tree, then drops and fixes in the mud.
steps.why: Mangroves grow in salty, waterlogged mud where a shed seed cannot germinate, so in Rhizophora the seed germinates on the tree and the seedling drops ready-grown.
common_mistakes: Writing Rhizobium (a bacterium) instead of Rhizophora.
steps.memory_tip: Rhizo = root: Rhizophora is the mangrove whose seedling drops with its root already formed.
steps.margin_note: The name Rhizophora alone earns this mark; the habit line is a safe extra.
